source: Scene-locked vertical (Instagram) FEATURE-PROMO reel for tap-to-read Scripture (library/verse-popup.js; commits 10e68b4b, 82f4660a, 1e99405b Greek, 3a6bb900 Hebrew). References on essays, Evidence Library cards, answers and mastery pages open an in-page popup with the verse (English: Berean Standard Bible, public domain) and an English/Greek (NT) or English/Hebrew (OT) toggle; the original-language view is word by word with transliteration and gloss, and tapping a word shows its lemma, dictionary meaning and decoded grammar (data: STEP TAGNT/TAHOT, Tyndale House, CC BY). All 8 screenshots are the LIVE site (tools/reel/shots/verse-popup.json): sc7 Romans 10:13 Greek with κυρίου selected; sc8 Isaiah 45:23 Hebrew with לִי ('to me') selected. Joel 2:32 was NOT used for Hebrew: ~8.5% of OT verses (1,969 / 23,145, measured 2026-09-27) have no Hebrew data - about half in 62 psalms, the rest in chapters whose English/Masoretic versification differs, incl. Joel 2:28-3:21 - and show 'Not available', so the reel says 'For most Old Testament verses, switch to Hebrew'. sc3 VO ported from library/jesus-is-yahweh.html:150; sc8 VO ported from the same essay ('where the LORD swears, "To me every knee shall bow…" (Isaiah 45:23)… The hymn bends that exclusive oath to Jesus').
voiceover: New on Apologia Daily: Bible references across the site are now tappable. Tap Joel 2:32, and the verse opens right there on the page. You never leave what you're reading. Then tap Romans 10, verses 9 to 13. That last line quotes Joel 2:32. Paul takes a text about calling on the covenant name of God and, without a word of apology, makes it a text about calling on Jesus. It works inside Evidence Library cards, without closing the card. On answer pages. And on Mastery Tracks. New Testament verses have a Greek button. Tap it, and the verse appears word by word, each Greek word with its transliteration and meaning. Tap a word for its dictionary form and grammar. Here, of the Lord is kyriou, from kyrios. For most Old Testament verses, switch to Hebrew, read right to left. In Isaiah 45:23 the LORD swears, To me every knee shall bow. The hymn in Philippians bends that exclusive oath to Jesus. All without leaving the page. The English is the Berean Standard Bible; the Greek and Hebrew come from STEP Bible at Tyndale House. Scripture, one tap away, at apologiadaily.com.
